title: Associative memory: total storage, active access and retention
objective: Prove a new, useful theorem giving an associative-memory architecture a quantified advantage in total memory, active read/write cost or retention over the strongest applicable published methods, while preserving high-dimensional queries and cross-coordinate binding.
relationship_to_previous_goal: This explicitly requested goal supersedes the blocked algebraic-complexity objective as the active research task. Historical records, manuscripts and priority uncertainties are preserved without claiming that the old objective was achieved.

plan.task: Specify fixed-feature overwrite and richer-query semantics; prove access/retention accounting lemmas; audit exact-regression and dynamic-linear-data-structure prior art.
Audit primary theorems for sparse inverse/local correction and dynamic graphical inference; classify what is already a known corollary.

Choose a concrete higher-dimensional binding workload for which dynamic dictionaries do not already solve the complete query specification. Seek a better constructive storage/access/retention bound, including changes to the active key set.
Derive a matching obstruction or a substantive separation against the strongest applicable published guarantee, including preprocessing, metadata, precision and encoder costs.
Produce a complete uniform proof and independent exact certificates; audit novelty and all boundary cases before training.
Prepare an honestly scoped manuscript only if novelty and impact gates pass. Use model experiments subsequently to assess the proven practical regime.

acceptance_criteria: A complete uniform proof with explicit hypotheses and a substantive new guarantee beyond the strongest primary baseline.
High-dimensional queries and useful cross-coordinate binding; no silent two-scalar bottleneck or arbitrary-label low-rank assumption.
All stored values, keys, codebooks, index/metadata, parameters, precision and preprocessing are charged.
Overwrite, forgetting, query robustness and horizon assumptions are explicit; no unlimited-precision capacity argument.
Exact reproducible certificates support the proof; numerical agreement alone does not establish it.
A defensible novelty boundary and a useful consequence support an honest paper; known reformulations and baseline separations alone do not complete the goal.

first_iteration.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Associative-memory goal: first proof iteration
proved_baselines: At least n*log2(alphabet_size) bits are needed to retain n independently replaceable values at known keys.
For fixed linear reads F and write support T, optimal off-target squared interference for a unit target change is (1-ell_i(T))/ell_i(T), with ell a projection leverage score.
If every row deletion of F has all column sets of size at most n-1 independent, an exact isolated overwrite needs at least n changed cells even with redundant state width.
An n-by-n Hadamard read basis has the sharp frontier n/t-1 for t changed cells.

For fixed sparse features with ||I-alpha*F*F^T||_infinity=rho<1, local polynomial correction gives uniform-in-horizon retention error at most rho^(L+1) times the bound on latest values. Metadata and the latest-value cache are charged.
Dyadic coefficient rounding plus bounded exact integer accumulators adds a fixed coefficient-error term without horizon-growing accumulation drift.

With fixed alpha and uniformly contracting active Gram matrices, a one-row key edit changes only encoding columns in the radius-L ball of the union of old/new overlap graphs. Local column replacement maintains the current polynomial encoding exactly under bounded-capacity insert/delete/replace and value edits.
first_iteration.classification: Elementary information/least-squares/sparse-inverse consequences and baselines. No superiority over the strongest existing methods or publishable novelty established.

next_actions: Complete the primary theorem audit for dynamic inference, sparse matrix-function approximations and dynamic kernel-graph algorithms before claiming a stronger architecture.
Specify a high-dimensional binding encoder and query-robustness workload that can realize sparse overlap and uniform contraction with useful total storage, index and precision costs.
Compare the dynamic local-polynomial guarantee with the strongest prior guarantee for exactly that workload; a Laplacian solution sketch is not automatically an individual memory read.
Reject the proposal if it is only an elementary polynomial-filter corollary or wins only against dense updates; do not launch neural training on those grounds.

dynamic_extension.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Second proof pass: local repair when keys change
dynamic_extension.uniform_guarantee: Current encoding identity and per-key maximum-error bound remain valid independently of horizon when all affected columns and integer contributions are replaced canonically.
conditions: Bounded feature/overlap support and charged incidence discovery
Bounded slot capacity with explicit inactive mask
Fixed global encoder parameters; edits change one key feature row
dynamic_extension.cost: At most b_L columns change; direct repair costs O(b_L^2*[L*(Delta+1)+k+k*value_width]) scalar operations plus discovery, metadata and finite-precision arithmetic costs. Index and coefficient storage is charged.

concrete_workload_gate.workload: Maintain bounded independent V_ij under point replacements; query a full-rank binding table by u^T*V*v with two vector-valued query parts.
concrete_workload_gate.exact_hardness: Unnormalized Boolean queries with absolute error below 1/2 contain Boolean vector-matrix-vector multiplication; do not promise truly subquadratic time with polynomial preprocessing without addressing the known OMv-conditional barrier.
concrete_workload_gate.approximate_baseline: For probability-vector queries and values in [-1,1], ordinary sampling uses O(epsilon^(-2)*log(1/delta)) table probes after paying sampler construction, while retaining all table entries and exact one-hot reads.
concrete_workload_gate.acceptance_requirement: Beat an applicable full-tradeoff baseline, including routing, precision and failure accounting; a dense-implementation saving or the classical sampler alone does not qualify.

second_iteration.previous_turn_classification: progress: supporting proofs, model, exact certificates and new active objective were preserved; goal not achieved
second_iteration.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Associative-memory goal: address geometry and signed writes
proved_supporting_results: Nonnegative unit feature rows satisfy (sum row_l1)^2 <= m*n*(1+R). Infinity-norm Gram contraction requires R<1, limiting effective positive address breadth at near-linear state width. Breadth is basis-dependent, not intrinsic input dimension.

Canonical normalized additive rank-one PSD recall has worst-label error at least 2*max(0,1-p/n), regardless of a quadratic feature state. This does not lower-bound delta, nonlinear or distributional recall.

MUB projector differences are exact rank-two dual writes for r*(p-1) fixed codeword associations. This is a known dual-frame/tomography consequence, has dense accesses and needs a precision/codebook audit beyond the dyadic controls.
The omitted-reference dual construction has a worst-case noise witness with read 1-p*t^2, so exact codeword retention alone does not provide a dimension-independent robust neighborhood.

Any quadratic reader with output bounded by B on every unit query and matched error epsilon<1 for every sign assignment satisfies n <= p*B^2/(1-epsilon)^2, even with nonlinear value encoding. This is a classical norm/margin consequence, not new publishable novelty.

second_iteration.decision: Park naive positive local-correction encoders and standalone MUB dual-writing as claimed contributions. Preserve their useful obstructions and controls. Seek a new robustness/access/retention tradeoff for an explicitly routed or nonlinear high-dimensional reader, compared on the same workload.
next_actions: Specify the richer reader and its allowed routing/nonlinearity, query perturbation norm, bounded-value semantics and active-key changes before proposing another experiment.

Seek a uniform robust retention guarantee with full read/write, index, codebook, precision and preprocessing costs; compare with the strongest applicable dictionary, sampling, kernel-regression and signed-attention baseline.

Investigate whether the dynamic local-repair theorem can support such a workload after charging routing/separation and truncation; reject a known inverse-filter or dual-frame corollary as the main contribution.
If a construction passes the prior-art and accounting gates, prove its tradeoff and an applicable obstruction before any new neural training; otherwise preserve the failure and iterate.

conditional_theorem.model: Encoded features (b_i,u_i), sparse local B and arbitrary r-dimensional shared U; independent latest V rows, fixed slot capacity and explicit inactive ghosts.
conditions: Fixed-depth symmetrically rounded polynomial C, positive definite with bounded infinity norm K
Explicit local/union-ball support and incidence bounds
One-row key/value/occupancy edits; global encoder and polynomial parameters fixed
conditional_theorem.guarantee: Maximum active-key value error <= [rho^(L+1)+(1+rho)*b*eta]*(1+M^2*K/c)*R, uniformly in overwrite horizon; explicit encoded-feature perturbation bound.
conditional_theorem.representation: Maintain latest V, C, Z=C*V, X=C*U, H, t, S0=B^T*Z, Y=B^T*X and small h=H^-1*t. Dense interpolation coefficients are implicit.
conditional_theorem.key_edits: C changes only in a union radius-L ball square. Replace every affected row contribution in X,Z,H,t,Y,S0 and recompute the small current solve.
conditional_theorem.value_edit_cost: O(k*b*v+r^2*v) scalar operations plus encoder/value-cache costs; all matrix sizes and bit lengths charged.
conditional_theorem.query_cost: O(k_q*(r+v)+r*v) scalar operations plus encoding/routing; no raw-input semantic margin is assumed for free.
conditional_theorem.precision: Canonical integer numerators on fixed grids; exact rational small solves with current-state bit bounds, not accumulated rounded inverse updates.
conditional_theorem.limitation: Encoded-space conditional extension of classical identities; no value-table compression, end-to-end high-dimensional semantic encoder, strongest-baseline superiority or novelty established.
